# Wave 1 (singleton, Task 1): CR → repair → SR → CR → commit

Checkout for every step: `/workspace/project`. `WAVE_BASE_SHA=1111111111111111111111111111111111111111` stays fixed.

## 1. Initial CR

Stage all deliverables, then record the CR tree (**T0**, keyed to wave 1). Run the fix-delta block in the branch checkout because this is an integrated review:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
FD_ROOT=/workspace/project
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"          # printed SHA = T0
```

```ts
subagent({ agent: "code-reviewer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<code-reviewer.md filled>
DESCRIPTION: Wave 1 (Task 1) summary from implementer report
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: <full Task 1 text>
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
Ask: production-ready?` })
```

- This payload has no `acceptance` field.
- It has no previous-report marker, so the report will carry no `TRAJECTORY:` line.

**Supplied result:** `FIX_FIRST`, with one Moderate finding and `Behaviour-change: yes`.

- This is CR review 1 with issues, so fix 1 is next.
- Fan-out is not possible. There is only one finding, and the wave is integrated but uncommitted, so it gets one in-place repair worker.

## 2. Repair dispatch (fix 1)

```ts
subagent({ agent: "implementer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<full Task 1 text + context>
## Review report (verbatim)
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
TEST_CONTRACT: <Task 1 Tests: block verbatim + Files: Create:/Test: paths>
<status protocol: DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT>` })
```

- The payload contains no commit or staging instruction.
- The worker returned `DONE` but committed `2222…` on its own. That is tolerated:
  - `WAVE_BASE_SHA` and `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE` stay unchanged.
  - The fold in step 6 absorbs the commit.
  - The fix delta is tree-based, so the moved HEAD does not affect it.

Rerun the scoped gate (supplied as passing):

```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs)
```

## 3. Repair-only delta

Stage, then record **T1** with the same block (`FD_ROOT=/workspace/project`). T1 is keyed to Task 1 for the SR.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
# fix-delta block -> T1
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T0> <T1>
```

- The delta should contain only the `src/parse.mjs` fix and the new `tests/error.test.mjs`.
- Do not use `1111..2222` or a working-tree diff in its place.

## 4. SR first (behaviour-change reroute)

```ts
subagent({ agent: "spec-reviewer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<full Task 1 text>
Absolute spec path: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md
Spec: anchors: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10 (read the ranges yourself)
Tests: block: <verbatim>   - Test: paths: tests/parse.test.mjs <as listed in Task 1>
Review the integrated checkout; start from the diff hunks, read every touched file in full, never run tests.
## Fix delta
<git diff --binary T0 T1 output>` })
```

- This SR runs as a first review: no `## Previous review report` marker and no trajectory block.
- It carries no test commands.
- Its ordinal continues the task's SR count, so it is SR review 2 (the initial SR was review 1).
- It reviews the implementation worktree directly, not a snapshot.

**Supplied result:** `COMPLIANT`.

## 5. CR re-review (CR review 2)

Stage, then record **T2** with the block, keyed to wave 1.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
# fix-delta block -> T2
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T0> <T2>
```

The delta runs from T0 (the tree at the prior CR's dispatch) to T2. Since SR is read-only, T2 should equal T1.

```ts
subagent({ agent: "code-reviewer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<code-reviewer.md filled>
DESCRIPTION: Wave 1 + fix 1 (reject empty string)
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: <full Task 1 text>
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes
<trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md, verbatim>
## Fix delta
<git diff --binary T0 T2 output>` })
```

**Supplied result:** `SHIP`. The verdict is clean, so the loop ends; no `TRAJECTORY:` line is expected on a clean report.

## 6. Fold, commit, complete

This happens only after the SR `COMPLIANT` and CR `SHIP` observations:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft "1111111111111111111111111111111111111111" \
  && git -C /workspace/project add -A \
  && git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Task 1: number parsing; reject empty string"
git -C /workspace/project status --porcelain   # expect clean tree
```

- The `reset --soft` folds the worker's `2222…` commit and all integrated changes into one wave commit on top of `1111…`.
- If the commit would be empty, stop instead of completing the task.

Then mark the task complete:

```ts
plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: <Task 1's positional index>, status: "complete" })
```

## Empty repair delta

If `git diff --binary T0 T1` were empty, the fix changed no tracked file. That includes a repair that only touched ignored files, or a worker that committed nothing new in content. HEAD moving to `2222…` would be irrelevant, because the delta compares trees.

In that case:
1. Dispatch no SR or CR re-review.
2. Count it as a failed attempt under "When a Subagent Fails".
3. Resend the prior CR report verbatim with "your fix changed no tracked file".
4. Stop after the existing two-attempt limit. Task 1 stays `in_progress` pending the human's decision.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
Below is a proposed sequence, not an execution transcript. `<FULL_TASK_1>` and `<TESTS_CONTRACT>` mean the available text pasted verbatim, not instructions for the child to locate it.

### 1. Stage and capture the initial CR tree

Run in the orchestrator shell. This helper runs the prescribed scratch-index block and propagates failures:

```bash
capture_tree() (
  FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
  FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
  cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || {
    rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1;
  }
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A &&
    GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
  FD_STATUS=$?
  rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
  exit "$FD_STATUS"
)

WAVE_BASE_SHA=1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
git -C /workspace/project add -A || exit 1
CR_TREE_1=$(capture_tree) || exit 1
printf 'wave1 initial-CR tree: %s\n' "$CR_TREE_1"
```

Dispatch the initial CR using the supplied code-reviewer template:

```js
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `Review production readiness; do not modify files.
DESCRIPTION: Task 1 parser implementation and tests, integrated after accepted SR.
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS:
<FULL_TASK_1>
<TESTS_CONTRACT>
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
Review staged and unstaged changes against BASE_SHA, including new files.
Check quality, architecture, test economy, requirements and plan deviations.
Return the standard code-review report and footer lines.`
})
```

The review source is **base versus current worktree**, not `HEAD~1..HEAD`. Its inspection commands are:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat "$WAVE_BASE_SHA" -- .
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary "$WAVE_BASE_SHA" -- .
```

### 2. Repair after the supplied `FIX_FIRST`

Use one in-place worker; this integrated, uncommitted wave must not fan out.

```js
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `Repair Task 1 in place.
<FULL_TASK_1>
<TESTS_CONTRACT>
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10
Fix the report below, adding tests/error.test.mjs as requested.
Use failing-test-first development for the behavior repair; self-review.
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
Run only that verification command.
Return explicitly DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, NEEDS_CONTEXT, or BLOCKED,
with changed files, test-contract results and concerns.

Prior review report, verbatim:
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes`
})
```

Do not instruct the repair worker to commit or stage.

Given its supplied `DONE` result and commit `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`, retain the original wave base. The moved HEAD does not become the review base.

```bash
(cd /workspace/project && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs) || exit 1
git -C /workspace/project add -A || exit 1
TASK1_SR_REPAIR_TREE=$(capture_tree) || exit 1
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary \
  "$CR_TREE_1" "$TASK1_SR_REPAIR_TREE"
```

That last command produces the **repair-only delta**, including the new tracked test despite the worker commit. Do not substitute a commit range.

### 3. Behavior-change gate: SR first, then CR

Dispatch SR against `/workspace/project`, continuing Task 1’s existing SR ordinal:

```js
subagent({
  agent: "spec-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `First review of this behavior-change repair.
<FULL_TASK_1>
<TESTS_CONTRACT>
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10
- Test: tests/parse.test.mjs
- Test: tests/error.test.mjs

## Fix delta
<verbatim binary diff produced above>

Review the fix against the task and anchored spec. Start from diff hunks;
read touched files in full. Never run tests.
Return the standard spec-review verdict.`
})
```

This SR has **no previous-review marker and no trajectory instruction**. Include any additional original `- Test:` paths verbatim.

After the supplied `COMPLIANT` observation:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A || exit 1
CR_TREE_2=$(capture_tree) || exit 1
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary "$CR_TREE_1" "$CR_TREE_2"
```

Dispatch CR with the same initial payload, unchanged base, `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE`, and scoped command, adding:

```text
## Fix delta
<verbatim binary diff just produced>

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes
```

Append the supplied **code-quality reviewer “Re-review: trajectory verdict” block verbatim**. Do not synthesize a trajectory or verdict.

### 4. Fold only after the supplied `SHIP`

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft "$WAVE_BASE_SHA" &&
git -C /workspace/project add -A &&
git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Fix numeric parsing and reject empty input"
```

Only on successful, nonempty commit, mark **the existing Task 1 tracker index complete**. The worker commit is folded into this single durable wave commit.

If the repair tree delta were empty, dispatch **no re-review**: count a failed attempt, resend the prior report with “your fix changed no tracked file,” and apply the existing two-attempt limit. A commit alone does not prove a tracked repair.
